You are ML Intern, an ML engineering assistant with 18 tools for training, fine-tuning, data processing, inference, and evaluation on the Hugging Face (HF) ecosystem. Your goal is to complete what the user requested with zero errors. You are fully autonomous — research, validate, implement, and deliver results without asking for unnecessary confirmation. # Your knowledge of HF libraries is outdated You do not know current APIs for TRL, Transformers, PEFT, Trackio, or other HF libraries. Your internal knowledge WILL produce wrong imports, wrong argument names, and wrong trainer configurations. Before writing any ML implementation code, start from the literature. The parallel research sub-agents can crawl papers, read their methodology sections, trace citation graphs, and extract the exact datasets and training recipes that produced published results. This is your primary advantage — use it. Your default workflow for any ML task: 1. Find the landmark paper(s) for the task or domain 2. Crawl their citation graphs to find recent downstream work 3. Read methodology sections (not abstracts) of the most promising papers — especially recent ones with strong results, lot of citations, and publications in high-impact conferences 4. Extract the recipe: what dataset, what training method, what hyperparameters produced those results 5. Validate and use those datasets for training ``` research({"task": "Literature crawl for [task]. Start from [paper/topic]. Crawl citation graph for recent downstream papers. Read their methodology sections (3, 4, 5) — extract the exact datasets, training methods, and hyperparameters that produced their best results. Attribute every finding to a specific result (e.g. 'Dataset X + method Y → 85.3% on benchmark Z'). Also find working code examples using current TRL/Transformers APIs.", "context": "User wants to [goal]. We need the best training recipe backed by published results."}) ``` The sub-agent knows how to use github_find_examples, github_read_file, explore_hf_docs, fetch_hf_docs, hf_inspect_dataset, and hf_papers (with citation_graph, read_paper, snippet_search, find_datasets). Be specific in your task description — name anchor papers or arxiv IDs when you have them. You can also call research tools directly (explore_hf_docs, github_read_file, etc.) for quick lookups. Skip research only for trivial non-code operations. # Mistakes you WILL make without research HALLUCINATED IMPORTS: You will import from modules that were renamed or removed. Example: old TRL trainer class names, deprecated Transformers APIs, wrong trackio config field names. Fix: read a current example script first. WRONG TRAINER ARGUMENTS: You will pass configuration arguments that don't exist in current trainer versions. Fix: fetch the actual trainer/config docs via explore_hf_docs + fetch_hf_docs. WRONG DATASET FORMAT: You will assume column names without checking. Training fails with KeyError. Fix: call hf_inspect_dataset or hub_repo_details and verify columns match the training method. DEFAULT TIMEOUT KILLS JOBS: You will leave timeout at the default 30m for training jobs. Training takes hours. The job gets killed and all progress is lost. Fix: set timeout based on model size (minimum 2h for any training). LOST MODELS: You will forget push_to_hub=True and hub_model_id in training config. Job storage is ephemeral — the filesystem is deleted when the job ends. Without push_to_hub, the trained model is permanently lost. BATCH FAILURES: You will submit all ablation/batch jobs at once without testing that one works first. All will fail for the same bug. Fix: submit ONE job first, verify it completes successfully, then submit the rest. SILENT DATASET SUBSTITUTION: When a requested dataset fails to load, you will silently switch to a different one without telling the user. Fix: if the requested dataset isn't available, tell the user and ask what to do. PREFER HUB KERNELS OVER COMPILING ATTENTION: Do NOT pip install 'flash-attn' to enable flash_attention_2 building from source can take many minutes to hours and often fails on the job's CUDA/PyTorch combo. Instead, use the HF `kernels` library (`pip install kernels`, already pulled in by recent TRL) and load a prebuilt attention kernel from the Hub via `attn_implementation`. Examples: `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(..., attn_implementation="kernels-community/flash-attn2")`, or `kernels-community/vllm-flash-attn3`, or `kernels-community/paged-attention`. With TRL/SFT scripts you can pass `--attn_implementation kernels-community/flash-attn2` on the CLI. Search additional kernels at https://huggingface.co/models?other=kernel. Only `pip install` extra packages (and document why) when no Hub kernel covers the need. SCOPE-CHANGING FIXES: Avoid at all costs! When you hit an error (especially OOM), you will try "creative" workarounds that change what the user asked for and/or change the training task itself — switching full SFT to LoRA on OOM, reducing max_length (silently truncates training data and changes what the model learns), disabling monitoring instead of fixing it. Do not do this. Fix errors with the minimal change that preserves the user's original request and are grounded in research and examples. If the original approach genuinely cannot work, explain why and ask the user for input before changing methods, sequence length, training approach or any other part of the task. # When writing ML code Required sequence before any training/fine-tuning/inference script: 1. Use `research` tool to find working examples, read docs, and get current API patterns 2. Validate dataset: hf_inspect_dataset or hub_repo_details to confirm column names and format 3. Validate model: hub_repo_details to confirm model exists, correct architecture/size/tokenizer Training logging: always set disable_tqdm=True, logging_strategy="steps", and logging_first_step=True in your TrainingArguments/SFTConfig so loss values are printed as plain text lines you can grep, not hidden inside tqdm progress bars. Dataset format requirements by training method: SFT: "messages", "text", or "prompt"/"completion" DPO: "prompt", "chosen", "rejected" GRPO: "prompt" # Trackio Trackio is natively integrated with Transformers Trainer and all TRL trainers — the built-in TrackioCallback handles init/log/finish. In TrainingArguments/SFTConfig/DPOConfig/GRPOConfig set: report_to="trackio" run_name="" # e.g. "sft_qwen3-4b_lr2e-5_bs128" project="" # keeps related runs grouped so you can compare them trackio_space_id="/mlintern-<8-char-id>" # creates a public dashboard Space `project` and `trackio_space_id` can also be set via TRACKIO_PROJECT / TRACKIO_SPACE_ID env vars. Alerts are how iterations decide what to change. Use trackio.alert(title, text, level) at every decision point in training. Levels: ERROR — stop and change approach (divergence, NaN, OOM) WARN — tweak hyperparameters (overfitting, early stopping, KL spike, reward collapse, slow convergence) INFO — milestones (training complete, target reached, checkpoint saved) Always include numeric values and an actionable suggestion in `text`, e.g. "loss=12.4 at step 200 — lr likely too high, try ×0.1". A future call must be able to parse it and act on it. To add alerts under Trainer/SFTTrainer/GRPOTrainer, pass a custom TrainerCallback via `callbacks=[...]` that calls trackio.alert() inside `on_log` (training metrics like loss, reward, kl) and `on_evaluate` (eval metrics — only available here, not in `on_log`). Keep each `if` simple: one metric, one threshold. Conditions stay easy to adjust between runs. Read alerts back between runs instead of parsing thousands of metric values. CLI — always use --json: trackio get alerts --project

--run --json trackio get alerts --project

--since --json # incremental polling trackio get run --project

--run --json trackio get metric --project

--run --metric --json trackio list runs --project

--json Python: api = trackio.Api(); api.alerts(

, run=, since=); api.runs(

) (each run has .name, .config, .alerts()). Drive the next config from prior alerts: diverged → lr × 0.1 overfitting → weight_decay × 10 or reduce capacity early stopping → lr × 0.5 or adjust schedule high accuracy → refine around current config Read prior config via api.runs(...).config and only mutate keys the alerts justify changing. # Data audit Before working with any dataset, audit it first. Do not assume you know what the data looks like — inspect it. Use hf_inspect_dataset to check: schema/columns, number of rows per split, value distributions for key columns, sample rows. Surface anything notable: class imbalance, missing values, unexpected formats, outliers, duplicate rows, etc. Looking at data is the best way to boost performance of any ML model plus it reduces the likelihood of failed jobs later. # When submitting a training job Before calling hf_jobs, output a pre-flight check: - Reference implementation: [which example you based this on] - Dataset format verified: [columns confirmed via hf_inspect_dataset/hub_repo_details] - push_to_hub=True and hub_model_id set - timeout: [value] (based on: [model size] on [hardware]) - Trackio monitoring included and deploying metrics to a public Space If you cannot fill in all items, stop and complete the missing steps first. For batch/ablation jobs: submit ONE job first. Check logs to confirm it starts training successfully. Only then submit the remaining jobs. Never submit all at once. Hardware sizing: 1-3B params: a10g-largex2 7-13B params: a100-large 30B+ params: l40sx4 or a100x4 70B+ params: a100x8 Note: a10g-small and a10g-large have the SAME 24GB GPU memory. The difference is CPU/RAM only. # Sandbox-first development A private cpu-basic sandbox is already available for normal code execution in each session. For non-trivial scripts, develop and test there before launching via hf_jobs: write script → pip install → test with small run using bash/read/write/edit → fix errors → launch via hf_jobs at scale Do NOT call sandbox_create before normal CPU work. Call sandbox_create only when you need GPU hardware or another non-default sandbox tier. Use GPU sandbox (t4-small minimum) when testing code that uses CUDA, bf16, or model loading. CPU sandboxes cannot test GPU code paths. # When a task has 3+ steps Use plan_tool to track progress. One task in_progress at a time. Mark completed immediately after finishing. Update frequently to show the user what you're doing. # Error recovery When something fails: - Diagnose the actual error. Read the full error message and logs. - Do not retry the exact same thing. Identify what needs to change. - If an API/import error: check documentation for the correct API. - If an OOM error: (1) reduce per_device_train_batch_size and increase gradient_accumulation_steps proportionally to keep effective batch size identical, (2) enable gradient_checkpointing=True, (3) upgrade to larger GPU (a10gx4→a100→a100x4→a100x8). Do NOT switch training methods (e.g. SFT→LoRA) or reduce max_length — those change what the user gets. If OOM happens in sandbox, create a new sandbox with larger GPU hardware. - Never change the user's requested approach (training method, dataset, model, sequence length) without explicit approval. - If a tool call fails repeatedly for the same reason: stop and try a different approach. - Never silently substitute resources (datasets, models) — tell the user if something isn't available. # Task completion Before ending your turn, verify: - Did you actually DO what the user asked, not just explain what you would do? - If something failed: did you diagnose and fix it, or at minimum explain what went wrong and ask for user input? - For training jobs: did you include a working Trackio dashboard URL? Do not stop after describing what you plan to do. Continue calling tools until the task is verifiably done. Do not mark plan tasks as completed if they failed or are only partially done. # Autonomous / headless mode When running autonomously (no human in the loop), you MUST follow these rules: NEVER respond with only text. Every response MUST include at least one tool call. If you have nothing to do, check the plan, verify outputs or plan ahead. A text-only response ends the agent loop permanently — there is no human to re-prompt you. NEVER STOP WORKING. Do NOT decide you are "done" while time remains. The human is not watching — they expect you to use the ENTIRE time budget productively. Do NOT ask "should I continue?" or "is this a good stopping point?" — there is nobody to answer. You run until the timer expires or you are manually killed. Your workflow is a loop, not a checklist. Once you have a working result, KEEP ITERATING: LOOP UNTIL TIME RUNS OUT: 1. Research the approach (read docs, find examples, check current APIs) 2. Implement the solution (write code, set up training) 3. Train and evaluate 4. Save the model to the required output location / push it to Hugging Face Hub 5. Improve: tune hyperparameters, try different data, adjust the training recipe, try a different approach entirely 6. Go to step 1 HYPERPARAMETER TUNING: Do not tune hyperparameters by hand one-at-a-time. Write a script that launches a sweep over a grid of values (learning rate, epochs, batch size, etc.) and evaluates each run automatically. One well-designed sweep script beats ten manual experiments. If you run out of ideas: go back to the literature. Crawl citation graphs deeper — find papers you haven't read yet, read their methodology sections, extract new datasets or training tricks. Look for papers that cite your current approach and improved on it. Try combining recipes from different papers. Re-read the task prompt for angles you missed. Re-read the training logs for clues. There is always a paper you haven't read yet, and it probably has a better dataset. Check the remaining time periodically with the timer command specified in the task prompt. Budget your time: reserve at least 10 minutes at the end for final evaluation and model saving. The task is NOT done until: - The required output exists (e.g. final model, metrics reached, dataset updated etc) - You have evaluated the model and confirmed it works # Communication - Be concise and direct. No filler, no restating what the user said. - One-word answers when appropriate for simple questions. - Always include direct Hub URLs when referencing models, datasets, Spaces, or jobs. - For errors: state what went wrong, why, and what you're doing to fix it. - Do not over-explain or present elaborate option menus for simple tasks. When the user's intent is clear, act on it. Present options only when there's genuine ambiguity. - Use the `notify` tool only when the user explicitly asked for out-of-band notifications or when the task clearly requires reporting to a configured messaging destination. Do not use it for routine chat updates. # Tool usage - Execute multiple independent tool calls in parallel when possible. - HF_TOKEN is automatically available in job secrets — no need to include it extra. - For training monitoring: include Trackio in the script and provide the dashboard URL. - For private/gated datasets: HF_TOKEN is needed — it's auto-loaded into job secrets. # CLI / Local mode You are running as a local CLI tool on the user's machine. There is NO sandbox — bash, read, write, and edit operate directly on the local filesystem. ## Summary: PortKit Minecraft Fine-Tuned Model via Tinker API

### What is PortKit?
PortKit is an AI-powered platform that converts Minecraft Java Edition mods (.jar) to Bedrock Edition add-ons (.mcaddon). It's a B2B product at **modporter.ai** with a multi-agent LangGraph pipeline. The project lives at `/home/alex/Projects/portkit/`.

### The Problem
PortKit relied on expensive API calls to GPT-4o/Claude for conversions. The goal was to fine-train an open-source model on Minecraft Java→Bedrock conversion to reduce cost and latency. Previous fine-tuning attempts were blocked by the local GPU (AMD RX 6600 XT, 8GB VRAM) — only tiny 0.5B-1.5B models could run.

### Key Decision: Use Tinker API
Alex had $150 credit for Tinker (Thinking Machines Lab's training API). Tinker provides cloud multi-GPU training with a Python SDK (`pip install tinker tinker-cookbook`). This allowed training on proper 8B models.

### Critical Constraint Discovered
**Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct** (the planned base model) is NOT supported on Tinker. The closest supported alternative is **Qwen/Qwen3-8B** (same model family, strong coding ability). This was discovered during research and forced a model swap.

### Training Data: MMSD Dataset
- **1,400 validated Java→Bedrock conversion pairs** at `ai-engine/mmsd/data/processed/validated_pairs.jsonl`
- Each pair has: `instruction`, `reasoning_trace`, `java_source`, `bedrock_source`
- 100% pass Mojmap validation (correct Java naming conventions)
- 97.8% fit within 4K tokens
- Data was synthetically generated by AI (not from real user conversions)

### Training Pipeline Executed

**Phase 1: SFT (Supervised Fine-Tuning)**
- Model: Qwen3-8B with LoRA rank=64
- Config: 3 epochs, LR=3e-4, batch_size=32, max_length=4096
- Used Tinker's high-level `tinker_cookbook.supervised.train` API
- Result: **59.8% loss reduction** (NLL: 0.70 → 0.28)
- One warning to note: the Qwen3 renderer doesn't satisfy the "extension property", so `TrainOnWhat.ALL_ASSISTANT_MESSAGES` produces a warning. It still trains but ideally each assistant message should be a separate conversation with `LAST_ASSISTANT_MESSAGE`.
- Checkpoint: `tinker://0c659d50-f836-5d81-9e44-4248ee4dddec:train:0/weights/final`

**Phase 2: GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization)**
- Resumed from SFT checkpoint (fresh optimizer, loaded weights only)
- Used Tinker's high-level `tinker_cookbook.rl.train` API with custom `Env` and `EnvGroupBuilder` subclasses
- Reward function: composite of structural alignment (35%), JSON validity (25%), content density (20%), length ratio (20%)
- Config: 50 steps, group_size=4, batch_size=4, LR=1e-4, max_completion_tokens=512
- Key API detail: `make_envs()` takes no arguments (not `n`). The Tinker API calls it without args and the builder's `group_size` determines how many envs to create.
- Result: **Reward 0.15 → 0.66 (4.3x improvement)**
- Checkpoint: `tinker://216b79ff-c3c0-5f71-9432-3348b7918f8d:train:0/weights/final`

**Low-level GRPO was abandoned** because the `importance_sampling` loss requires 4 fields in `loss_fn_inputs` (including `mask` and `logprobs`), not just `target_tokens` and `advantages`. The cookbook's `rl_loop.py` recipe is outdated — the high-level `rl/train.py` handles this correctly internally.

### Final Evaluation (20 held-out samples)

| Model | Reward | Manifest% | JS% | BLEU | Structural |
|-------|--------|-----------|-----|------|-----------|
| Baseline (Qwen3-8B) | 0.070 | 0% | 0% | 0.282 | 0.000 |
| SFT only | 0.152 | 60% | 60% | 0.423 | 0.149 |
| **SFT+GRPO** | **0.618** | **100%** | **100%** | 0.290 | 0.279 |

Baseline generated zero manifests and zero JS. Fine-tuned model generates both 100% of the time. Structural alignment and BLEU are still weak — the model produces plausible Minecraft output but doesn't closely match ground truth.

### Published Model
**https://huggingface.co/alexchapin/portkit-qwen3-8b-minecraft** — merged model (base + LoRA, 16.4GB)

### Files Created
All in `ai-engine/mmsd/tinker/`:
- `TINKER_TRAINING_PLAN.md` — Full plan with budget breakdown
- `convert_data.py` — Converts MMSD JSONL → Tinker conversations JSONL format
- `reward.py` — Composite reward functions (structural, BLEU, JSON validity, density)
- `sft_train.py` — SFT via Tinker (high-level and low-level modes)
- `grpo_train.py` — GRPO via Tinker low-level loop (note: has the mask bug, see below)
- `evaluate.py` — Baseline vs fine-tuned evaluation
- `export_model.py` — Downloads and pushes to HF Hub
- `data/train.jsonl` (1,260 samples) and `data/val.jsonl` (140 samples)

### Known Issues / Context for Future Work
1. **`grpo_train.py` has outdated low-level GRPO code** that's missing the `mask` field. The working GRPO was done inline with the high-level API. The script needs to be updated or replaced with the `Env`/`EnvGroupBuilder` pattern.
2. **General code mix (12%) was planned but never run** — `convert_data.py --add-general-mix` flag exists but wasn't used in the training run. This may help prevent catastrophic forgetting.
3. **max_completion_length=512 during GRPO** is too short — ground truth averages ~2K tokens. This limits reward signal quality.
4. **BLEU is low (0.29)** — the model generates structurally valid output but content doesn't closely match references. This is the biggest gap to close.
5. **Tinker API quirks learned**: `create_training_client_from_state()` (not `create_lora_training_client_from_saved_state`), `build_generation_prompt()` (not `build_sampling_prompt`), `result().sequences` (not `result().samples`), sampler weights path needed for downloads (not training weights path).
6. **Budget remaining**: roughly $70-100 of the $150 credit remains unused.

import asyncio, json, chz
import tinker
from tinker_cookbook import model_info
from tinker_cookbook.rl import train as rl_train
from tinker_cookbook.rl.types import (
    RLDataset, RLDatasetBuilder, Env, EnvGroupBuilder, StepResult
)
from tinker_cookbook.renderers import get_renderer, Message
from tinker_cookbook.tokenizer_utils import get_tokenizer
from datetime import datetime
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, 'ai-engine/mmsd/tinker')
from reward import compute_reward

model_name = 'Qwen/Qwen3-8B'
renderer_name = model_info.get_recommended_renderer_name(model_name)
tokenizer = get_tokenizer(model_name)
renderer = get_renderer(renderer_name, tokenizer)

conversations = []
with open('ai-engine/mmsd/tinker/data/train.jsonl') as f:
    for line in f:
        if line.strip():
            conversations.append(json.loads(line))

prompts_data = []
for conv in conversations:
    msgs = []
    reference = ''
    for msg in conv['messages']:
        if msg['role'] == 'assistant':
            reference = msg['content']
        else:
            msgs.append(msg)
    prompts_data.append((msgs, reference))
print(f'Loaded {len(prompts_data)} prompts')

class PortKitEnv(Env):
    def __init__(self, messages, reference, renderer):
        self.messages = [Message(role=m['role'], content=m['content']) for m in messages]
        self.reference = reference
        self.renderer = renderer
        self.tokenizer = renderer.tokenizer

    async def initial_observation(self):
        prompt = self.renderer.build_generation_prompt(self.messages)
        return prompt, self.renderer.get_stop_sequences()

    async def step(self, action, *, extra=None):
        response = self.tokenizer.decode(action, skip_special_tokens=True)
        reward = compute_reward(response, self.reference)
        return StepResult(
            reward=reward, episode_done=True,
            next_observation=tinker.ModelInput.from_ints([]),
            next_stop_condition=[],
        )

class PortKitEnvGroupBuilder(EnvGroupBuilder):
    def __init__(self, messages, reference, renderer, group_size=8):
        self.messages = messages
        self.reference = reference
        self.renderer = renderer
        self.group_size = group_size

    async def make_envs(self):
        return [PortKitEnv(self.messages, self.reference, self.renderer) for _ in range(self.group_size)]

@chz.chz
class PortKitRLDatasetBuilder(RLDatasetBuilder):
    renderer_name: str = renderer_name
    model_name_for_tokenizer: str = model_name
    batch_size: int = 8
    group_size: int = 8
    seed: int = 42

    async def __call__(self):
        import random
        rnd = random.Random(self.seed)
        _renderer = get_renderer(self.renderer_name, get_tokenizer(self.model_name_for_tokenizer))

        builders = []
        for msgs, ref in prompts_data:
            builders.append(PortKitEnvGroupBuilder(msgs, ref, _renderer, self.group_size))
        rnd.shuffle(builders)

        train_builders = builders[:int(len(builders) * 0.9)]
        test_builders = builders[int(len(builders) * 0.9):]

        class SimpleRLDataset(RLDataset):
            def __init__(self, data, bs):
                self.data = data
                self.bs = bs
            def get_batch(self, index):
                start = index * self.bs
                return self.data[start:start+self.bs]
            def __len__(self):
                return len(self.data) // self.bs

        train_ds = SimpleRLDataset(train_builders, self.batch_size)
        test_ds = SimpleRLDataset(test_builders, self.batch_size) if len(test_builders) >= self.batch_size else None
        print(f'Train batches: {len(train_ds)}, Test batches: {len(test_ds) if test_ds else 0}')
        return train_ds, test_ds

timestamp = datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')
log_path = f'ai-engine/mmsd/tinker/logs/grpo2_qwen3-8b_{timestamp}'

# Resume from GRPO final checkpoint (the best model so far)
grpo_checkpoint = 'tinker://216b79ff-c3c0-5f71-9432-3348b7918f8d:train:0/weights/final'

config = chz.Blueprint(rl_train.Config).apply({
    'log_path': log_path,
    'model_name': model_name,
    'renderer_name': renderer_name,
    'dataset_builder': PortKitRLDatasetBuilder(),
    'learning_rate': 5e-5,
    'max_tokens': 2048,
    'lora_rank': 64,
    'temperature': 0.8,
    'save_every': 25,
    'eval_every': 0,
    'max_steps': 200,
    'load_checkpoint_path': grpo_checkpoint,
})

print(f'Starting GRPO v2 from previous GRPO checkpoint')
print(f'  Checkpoint: {grpo_checkpoint}')
print(f'  Steps: 200, Batch: 8, Group: 8, Max tokens: 2048')
print(f'  LR: 5e-5 (lower for continued training)')
print(f'  Log path: {log_path}')

config_obj = config.make()
asyncio.run(rl_train.main(config_obj))

print(f'GRPO v2 training complete! Logs at {log_path}')

import asyncio, json, chz
import tinker
from tinker_cookbook import model_info
from tinker_cookbook.rl import train as rl_train
from tinker_cookbook.rl.types import (
    RLDataset, RLDatasetBuilder, Env, EnvGroupBuilder, StepResult
)
from tinker_cookbook.renderers import get_renderer, Message
from tinker_cookbook.tokenizer_utils import get_tokenizer
from datetime import datetime
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, 'ai-engine/mmsd/tinker')
from reward import compute_reward

model_name = 'Qwen/Qwen3-8B'
renderer_name = model_info.get_recommended_renderer_name(model_name)
tokenizer = get_tokenizer(model_name)
renderer = get_renderer(renderer_name, tokenizer)

conversations = []
with open('ai-engine/mmsd/tinker/data/train.jsonl') as f:
    for line in f:
        if line.strip():
            conversations.append(json.loads(line))

prompts_data = []
for conv in conversations:
    msgs, reference = [], ''
    for msg in conv['messages']:
        if msg['role'] == 'assistant': reference = msg['content']
        else: msgs.append(msg)
    prompts_data.append((msgs, reference))
print(f'Loaded {len(prompts_data)} prompts')

class PortKitEnv(Env):
    def __init__(self, messages, reference, renderer):
        self.messages = [Message(role=m['role'], content=m['content']) for m in messages]
        self.reference = reference
        self.renderer = renderer
        self.tokenizer = renderer.tokenizer

    async def initial_observation(self):
        prompt = self.renderer.build_generation_prompt(self.messages)
        return prompt, self.renderer.get_stop_sequences()

    async def step(self, action, *, extra=None):
        response = self.tokenizer.decode(action, skip_special_tokens=True)
        reward = compute_reward(response, self.reference)
        return StepResult(
            reward=reward, episode_done=True,
            next_observation=tinker.ModelInput.from_ints([]),
            next_stop_condition=[],
        )

class PortKitEnvGroupBuilder(EnvGroupBuilder):
    def __init__(self, messages, reference, renderer, group_size=8):
        self.messages = messages
        self.reference = reference
        self.renderer = renderer
        self.group_size = group_size

    async def make_envs(self):
        return [PortKitEnv(self.messages, self.reference, self.renderer) for _ in range(self.group_size)]

@chz.chz
class PortKitRLDatasetBuilder(RLDatasetBuilder):
    renderer_name: str = renderer_name
    model_name_for_tokenizer: str = model_name
    batch_size: int = 8
    group_size: int = 8
    seed: int = 42

    async def __call__(self):
        import random
        rnd = random.Random(self.seed)
        _renderer = get_renderer(self.renderer_name, get_tokenizer(self.model_name_for_tokenizer))

        builders = [PortKitEnvGroupBuilder(msgs, ref, _renderer, self.group_size) for msgs, ref in prompts_data]
        rnd.shuffle(builders)

        train_builders = builders[:int(len(builders) * 0.9)]

        class SimpleRLDataset(RLDataset):
            def __init__(self, data, bs):
                self.data = data
                self.bs = bs
            def get_batch(self, index):
                start = index * self.bs
                return self.data[start:start+self.bs]
            def __len__(self):
                return len(self.data) // self.bs

        train_ds = SimpleRLDataset(train_builders, self.batch_size)
        print(f'Train batches: {len(train_ds)}')
        return train_ds, None

            conversations.append(json.loads(line))

@chz.chz
class StageBDatasetBuilder(SFTDatasetBuilder):
    model_name: str = model_name
    renderer_name: str = renderer_name
    max_length: int = 4096
    seed: int = 42

    async def __call__(self):
        import random
        rnd = random.Random(self.seed)
        _conversations = conversations.copy()
        rnd.shuffle(_conversations)

        # Convert to Message format
        all_data = []
        for conv in _conversations:
            msgs = [Message(role=m['role'], content=m['content']) for m in conv['messages']]
            all_data.append(msgs)

        split = int(len(all_data) * 0.9)
        train_data = all_data[:split]
        test_data = all_data[split:]

        return SFTDataset(train_data=train_data, test_data=test_data)

class SupervisedDataset:
    """Abstract base for datasets used in supervised learning.

    Subclasses must implement ``get_batch`` and ``__len__``.  ``set_epoch``
    may be overridden to shuffle data between epochs.
    """

    def get_batch(self, index: int) -> list[tinker.Datum]:
        """Return a batch of training Datum objects at the given index.

        Args:
            index (int): The batch index.

        Returns:
            list[tinker.Datum]: The training datums for this batch.

        raise NotImplementedError

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        """Return the number of batches in the dataset."""

import asyncio, json, chz
import tinker
from tinker_cookbook import model_info
from tinker_cookbook.rl import train as rl_train
from tinker_cookbook.rl.types import RLDataset, RLDatasetBuilder, Env, EnvGroupBuilder, StepResult
from tinker_cookbook.renderers import get_renderer, Message
from tinker_cookbook.tokenizer_utils import get_tokenizer
from datetime import datetime
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, 'ai-engine/mmsd/tinker')
from reward import compute_reward

model_name = 'Qwen/Qwen3-8B'
renderer_name = model_info.get_recommended_renderer_name(model_name)
tokenizer = get_tokenizer(model_name)
renderer = get_renderer(renderer_name, tokenizer)

# Use Stage B SFT data (direct output format)
conversations = []
with open('ai-engine/mmsd/tinker/data/stage_b_train.jsonl') as f:
    for line in f:
        if line.strip():
            conversations.append(json.loads(line))

prompts_data = []
for conv in conversations:
    msgs, reference = [], ''
    for msg in conv['messages']:
        if msg['role'] == 'assistant': reference = msg['content']
        else: msgs.append(msg)
    prompts_data.append((msgs, reference))
print(f'Loaded {len(prompts_data)} prompts')

class PortKitEnv(Env):
    def __init__(self, messages, reference, renderer):
        self.messages = [Message(role=m['role'], content=m['content']) for m in messages]
        self.reference = reference
        self.renderer = renderer
        self.tokenizer = renderer.tokenizer

    async def initial_observation(self):
        prompt = self.renderer.build_generation_prompt(self.messages)
        return prompt, self.renderer.get_stop_sequences()

    async def step(self, action, *, extra=None):
        response = self.tokenizer.decode(action, skip_special_tokens=True)
        reward = compute_reward(response, self.reference)
        return StepResult(reward=reward, episode_done=True, next_observation=tinker.ModelInput.from_ints([]), next_stop_condition=[])

class PortKitEnvGroupBuilder(EnvGroupBuilder):
    def __init__(self, messages, reference, renderer, group_size=8):
        self.messages, self.reference, self.renderer, self.group_size = messages, reference, renderer, group_size
    async def make_envs(self):
        return [PortKitEnv(self.messages, self.reference, self.renderer) for _ in range(self.group_size)]

@chz.chz
class PortKitRLDatasetBuilder(RLDatasetBuilder):
    renderer_name: str = renderer_name
    model_name_for_tokenizer: str = model_name
    batch_size: int = 8
    group_size: int = 8
    seed: int = 42

    async def __call__(self):
        import random
        rnd = random.Random(self.seed)
        _renderer = get_renderer(self.renderer_name, get_tokenizer(self.model_name_for_tokenizer))
        builders = [PortKitEnvGroupBuilder(msgs, ref, _renderer, self.group_size) for msgs, ref in prompts_data]
        rnd.shuffle(builders)
        train_builders = builders[:int(len(builders) * 0.9)]
        class SimpleRLDataset(RLDataset):
            def __init__(self, data, bs):
                self.data, self.bs = data, bs
            def get_batch(self, index):
                return self.data[index*self.bs:(index+1)*self.bs]
            def __len__(self):
                return len(self.data) // self.bs
        train_ds = SimpleRLDataset(train_builders, self.batch_size)
        print(f'Train batches: {len(train_ds)}')
        return train_ds, None

timestamp = datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')
log_path = f'ai-engine/mmsd/tinker/logs/grpo3_stageb_qwen3-8b_{timestamp}'

# Load from Stage B SFT checkpoint
stage_b_checkpoint = 'tinker://74954426-1586-52f2-a6cd-b38418134483:train:0/weights/final'

config = chz.Blueprint(rl_train.Config).apply({
    'log_path': log_path,
    'model_name': model_name,
    'renderer_name': renderer_name,
    'dataset_builder': PortKitRLDatasetBuilder(),
    'learning_rate': 3e-5,  # Lower LR for refinement
    'max_tokens': 2048,
    'lora_rank': 64,
    'temperature': 0.7,
    'save_every': 25,
    'eval_every': 0,
    'max_steps': 75,  # Fewer steps for refinement
    'load_checkpoint_path': stage_b_checkpoint,
})

print(f'GRPO v3 from Stage B SFT checkpoint')
print(f'  Checkpoint: {stage_b_checkpoint}')
print(f'  Steps: 75, Batch: 8, Group: 8, Max tokens: 2048, LR: 3e-5')
print(f'  Log: {log_path}')

config_obj = config.make()
asyncio.run(rl_train.main(config_obj))
print(f'GRPO v3 complete! Logs at {log_path}')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Export Tinker-trained PortKit model to HuggingFace Hub
======================================================
Downloads the trained LoRA weights from Tinker, merges with base model,
and pushes to HuggingFace Hub.

Usage:
    python export_model.py \
        --checkpoint-path /path/to/checkpoint/final \
        --hub-repo alexchapin/portkit-coder-7b-merged \

    python export_model.py --checkpoint-path /path/to/checkpoint/final

import argparse

                        help="HuggingFace Hub repo ID")
    parser.add_argument("--push-merged", action="store_true",
                        help="Merge LoRA + base and push full model")
    parser.add_argument("--push-lora-only", action="store_true",
                        help="Push only the LoRA adapter weights")
    parser.add_argument("--local-dir", type=str, default=None,
                        help="Download to local directory instead of Hub")
    parser.add_argument("--private", action="store_true",
                        help="Make HF repo private")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    try:

        print("  export HF_TOKEN='your-hf-token'")
        sys.exit(1)

    print("=" * 60)
    print("PortKit Model Export")
    print("=" * 60)
    print(f"Checkpoint: {args.checkpoint_path}")
    print(f"Hub repo: {args.hub_repo}")
    print()

    # Download checkpoint archive
    print("Downloading checkpoint from Tinker...")
    service_client = tinker.ServiceClient()
    rest_client = service_client.create_rest_client()

    if args.local_dir:
        local_dir = Path(args.local_dir)

        download.download_checkpoint(args.checkpoint_path, str(local_dir))
        print(f"Downloaded to {local_dir}")
        return

    if args.push_merged:
        print("Building merged model (base + LoRA)...")
        model_path = build_hf_model(args.checkpoint_path)

        print(f"Publishing merged model to {args.hub_repo}...")
        publish_to_hf_hub(
            model_path=model_path,
            repo_id=args.hub_repo,
            token=hf_token,
            private=args.private,
        )
        print(f"✓ Merged model published to https://huggingface.co/{args.hub_repo}")

    if args.push_lora_only:
        lora_repo = args.hub_repo + "-lora"

(*, base_model: 'str', adapter_path: 'str', output_path: 'str', dtype: 'str' = 'bfloat16', trust_remote_code: 'bool | None' = None, merge_strategy: 'str' = 'auto', dequantize: 'bool' = False, quantize: 'str | None' = None, serving_format: 'str | None' = None, device: 'str | None' = None) -> 'None'

def build_hf_model(
    *,
    base_model: str,
    adapter_path: str,
    output_path: str,
    dtype: str = "bfloat16",
    trust_remote_code: bool | None = None,
    merge_strategy: str = "auto",
    dequantize: bool = False,
    quantize: str | None = None,
    serving_format: str | None = None,
    device: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Build a complete HuggingFace model from Tinker LoRA adapter weights.

    Merges the LoRA adapter into the base model and saves the result as a
    standard HuggingFace model directory, compatible with vLLM, SGLang, TGI,
    or any HuggingFace-compatible inference framework.

    Args:
        base_model: HuggingFace model name (e.g. ``"Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B"``)
            or local path to a saved HuggingFace model.
        adapter_path: Local path to the Tinker adapter directory. Must contain
            ``adapter_model.safetensors`` and ``adapter_config.json``.
        output_path: Directory where the merged model will be saved. Must not
            already exist.
        dtype: Data type for loading the base model. One of ``"bfloat16"``
            (default), ``"float16"``, or ``"float32"``. Use ``"float32"``
            for maximum precision during merge. Only used by
            ``merge_strategy="full"``; the shard strategy preserves the
            on-disk dtype of each tensor.
        trust_remote_code: Whether to trust remote code when loading HF
            models. Required for some newer model architectures (e.g.
            Qwen3.5). If ``None`` (default), falls back to the
            ``HF_TRUST_REMOTE_CODE`` environment variable, then ``False``.
        merge_strategy: Controls how the merge is performed. ``"auto"``
            (default) uses shard-by-shard processing for lower peak memory.
            ``"shard"`` forces shard-by-shard (fails if shards can't be
            resolved). ``"full"`` forces full-model loading (original
            behavior, higher memory but simpler).
        dequantize: If ``True``, dequantize quantized base model weights
            before merging. Not yet implemented for the standard merge path,
            but used internally by the quantized export path for models with
            native FP8 weights (e.g. DeepSeek V3.1).
        quantize: Output quantization method. Currently supported:
            ``"experts-fp8"`` — quantize routed expert weights to FP8 with
            blockwise scaling. Requires ``serving_format`` to be set.
            ``None`` (default) — no quantization.
        serving_format: Serving framework format for quantization metadata.
            Currently supported: ``"vllm"`` — write compressed-tensors
            config for vLLM. Required when ``quantize`` is set.
            ``None`` (default) — no serving-specific metadata.
        device: Device for quantization math. ``"cpu"`` forces CPU,
            ``"cuda"`` or ``"cuda:0"`` etc. uses GPU for faster
            quantization. ``None`` (default) auto-detects: uses CUDA
            if available, otherwise CPU. Only affects the quantized
            export path (``quantize`` is set).

    Example::

        from tinker_cookbook import weights

        weights.build_hf_model(
            base_model="Qwen/Qwen3-8B",
            adapter_path="./adapter",
            output_path="./merged_model",
        )

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If adapter files are missing.
        FileExistsError: If output_path already exists.
        KeyError: If adapter config is malformed.
        ValueError: If tensor shapes are incompatible during merge, or
            if ``dtype``, ``merge_strategy``, ``quantize``, or
            ``serving_format`` is not a recognized value, or if
            ``quantize`` and ``serving_format`` are not both set/unset.
        NotImplementedError: If ``dequantize=True`` on the standard merge path.
    """
    # --- Validate quantize / serving_format ---
    if quantize is not None and quantize not in _VALID_QUANTIZE:
        raise ConfigurationError(
            f"Unsupported quantize={quantize!r}. Choose from: {sorted(_VALID_QUANTIZE)}"
        )
    if serving_format is not None and serving_format not in _VALID_SERVING_FORMATS:
        raise ConfigurationError(
            f"Unsupported serving_format={serving_format!r}. "
            f"Choose from: {sorted(_VALID_SERVING_FORMATS)}"
        )
    if quantize is not None and serving_format is None:
        raise ConfigurationError(
            f"quantize={quantize!r} requires serving_format to be set "
            f"(e.g. serving_format='vllm') to write scale metadata."
        )
    if serving_format is not None and quantize is None:
        raise ConfigurationError(
            f"serving_format={serving_format!r} requires quantize to be set "
            f"(e.g. quantize='experts-fp8'). Serving format without quantization is meaningless."
        )
    if quantize == "experts-fp8" and dtype != "bfloat16":
        raise ConfigurationError(
            f"quantize='experts-fp8' requires dtype='bfloat16', got dtype={dtype!r}."
        )

    # --- Validate standard params ---
    if dequantize and quantize is None:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "dequantize is not yet supported for the standard merge path. "
            "Use quantize='experts-fp8' for models with native FP8 weights."
        )
    if dtype not in _DTYPE_MAP:
        raise ConfigurationError(
            f"Unsupported dtype {dtype!r}. Choose from: {list(_DTYPE_MAP.keys())}"
        )
    if merge_strategy not in _VALID_STRATEGIES:
        raise ConfigurationError(
            f"Unsupported merge_strategy {merge_strategy!r}. "
            f"Choose from: {sorted(_VALID_STRATEGIES)}"
        )

    resolved_trust = resolve_trust_remote_code(trust_remote_code)

    # Load model config for model-family detection (lightweight, no weight download).
    config_dict = load_config_dict(base_model, trust_remote_code=resolved_trust)

    # --- Warn if native FP8 model without quantized export ---
    if quantize is None and _has_native_fp8(config_dict):
        logger.warning(
            "This model appears to have native FP8 weights "
            "(quantization_config.quant_method='fp8'). "
            "The standard merge path will apply LoRA deltas directly to FP8 tensors, "
            "which may produce incorrect results due to FP8 precision loss. "
            "Consider using quantize='experts-fp8' and serving_format='vllm' "
            "for correct FP8-aware merging."
        )

    # --- Quantized export path ---
    if quantize is not None:
        resolved_device = (
            device if device is not None else ("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
        )
        from tinker_cookbook.weights._export._quantized import build_quantized

        model_dir = resolve_model_dir(base_model)
        build_quantized(
            base_model=base_model,
            adapter_path=adapter_path,
            output_path=output_path,
            trust_remote_code=resolved_trust,
            model_dir=model_dir,
            config_dict=config_dict,
            serving_format=serving_format,  # type: ignore[arg-type]  # validated non-None above
            device=resolved_device,
        )
        return

    # --- Standard merge path ---
    strategy = _resolve_strategy(merge_strategy)

    if strategy == "full":
        from tinker_cookbook.weights._export._full import build_full

        build_full(
            base_model=base_model,
            adapter_path=adapter_path,
            output_path=output_path,
            dtype=dtype,
            torch_dtype=_DTYPE_MAP[dtype],
            trust_remote_code=resolved_trust,
            config_dict=config_dict,
        )
    else:
        if dtype != "bfloat16":
            logger.warning(
                "dtype=%r only applies to merge_strategy='full'. "
                "The shard strategy preserves each tensor's on-disk dtype. "
                "Pass merge_strategy='full' to control output precision.",
                dtype,
            )

        from tinker_cookbook.weights._export._shard import build_sharded

        resolved_device = (
            device if device is not None else ("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
        )
        model_dir = resolve_model_dir(base_model)
        build_sharded(
            base_model=base_model,
            adapter_path=adapter_path,
            output_path=output_path,
            trust_remote_code=resolved_trust,
            model_dir=model_dir,
            config_dict=config_dict,
            device=resolved_device,
        )

    extracts it with security validation (rejects symlinks and path
    traversal).

export $(grep TINKER_API_KEY /home/alex/Projects/portkit/.env) && cd /home/alex/Projects/portkit && .venv/bin/python -c "
import json, sys
sys.path.insert(0, 'ai-engine/mmsd/tinker')
from reward import compute_reward
from tinker_cookbook import model_info
from tinker_cookbook.renderers import get_renderer, Message
from tinker_cookbook.tokenizer_utils import get_tokenizer
from tinker_cookbook.checkpoint_utils import create_training_client_from_state
import tinker

model_name = 'Qwen/Qwen3-8B'
renderer_name = model_info.get_recommended_renderer_name(model_name)
tokenizer = get_tokenizer(model_name)
renderer = get_renderer(renderer_name, tokenizer)

# Load 20 eval samples
eval_data = []
with open('ai-engine/mmsd/tinker/data/stage_b_val.jsonl') as f:
    for line in f:
        if line.strip():
            eval_data.append(json.loads(line))

# Take first 20
eval_data = eval_data[:20]
print(f'Evaluating on {len(eval_data)} samples')

# Create sampling client from GRPO v3 checkpoint
checkpoint = 'tinker://ffa0bfc7-f373-5af3-aeab-9773784a51a0:train:0/sampler_weights/final'
print(f'Loading checkpoint: {checkpoint}')
client = create_training_client_from_state(checkpoint)

# Evaluate
rewards = []
for i, sample in enumerate(eval_data):
    msgs = [Message(role=m['role'], content=m['content']) for m in sample['messages'] if m['role'] != 'assistant']
    reference = ''
    for m in sample['messages']:
        if m['role'] == 'assistant':
            reference = m['content']
    
    prompt = renderer.build_generation_prompt(msgs)
    result = client.sample(prompt, max_tokens=2048, temperature=0.0)
    response = tokenizer.decode(result.sequences[0], skip_special_tokens=True)
    
    reward = compute_reward(response, reference)
    rewards.append(reward)
    
    # Check key properties
    has_json = 'manifest' in response.lower() or '{' in response
    has_js = 'function' in response.lower() or 'const ' in response.lower() or 'let ' in response.lower()
    print(f'  Sample {i}: Reward={reward:.4f}, JSON={has_json}, JS={has_js}')

print(f'\\nAverage reward: {sum(rewards)/len(rewards):.4f}')
print(f'Min: {min(rewards):.4f}, Max: {max(rewards):.4f}')
" 2>&1","description":"Evaluate GRPO v3 model on held-out data","timeout":600}

        continue

    if self_reward < 0.15:

def load_general_code_sample(sample_size: int = 200, seed: int = 42) -> list[dict]:
    """Load general Java/JS code data for forgetting mitigation (12% mix).

    Uses m-a-p/CodeFeedback-Filtered-Instruction from HuggingFace.
    Falls back to empty list if dataset not available.
    """
    try:
        from datasets import load_dataset

        print("Loading general code dataset (m-a-p/CodeFeedback-Filtered-Instruction)...")
        ds = load_dataset(
            "m-a-p/CodeFeedback-Filtered-Instruction", split="train", streaming=True
        )

        java_js_samples = []
        for row in ds:
            lang = row.get("lang", "")
            if lang in ("java", "javascript"):
                java_js_samples.append(row)
                if len(java_js_samples) >= sample_size * 3:
                    break

        random.seed(seed)
        random.shuffle(java_js_samples)
        selected = java_js_samples[:sample_size]

        conversations = []
        for row in selected:
            conversations.append({
                "messages": [
                    {"role": "user", "content": row["query"]},
                    {"role": "assistant", "content": row["answer"]},
                ]
            })
        print(f"  Loaded {len(conversations)} general code samples")
        return conversations

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  Warning: Could not load general code data: {e}")
        print("  Proceeding with MMSD data only (no forgetting mitigation mix)")
        return []

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""
     3	PortKit Reward Functions for Tinker GRPO Training
     4	===================================================
     5	Custom reward functions for evaluating Minecraft Java→Bedrock mod conversion quality.
     6	
     7	These reward functions are used during GRPO training to score model completions
     8	against ground truth Bedrock add-on outputs.
     9	"""
    10	
    11	import json
    12	import re
    13	from typing import Optional
    14	
    15	
    16	def extract_manifest(text: str) -> Optional[str]:
    17	    """Extract manifest.json content from model output."""
    18	    json_blocks = re.findall(r"```json\s*(.*?)\s*```", text, re.DOTALL)
    19	    for block in json_blocks:
    20	        if "format_version" in block or "header" in block:
    21	            return block.strip()
    22	    section = re.search(r"## Bedrock Add-on Output(.*?)(?:##|$)", text, re.DOTALL)
    23	    if section:
    24	        m = re.search(r'\{[^{}]*"format_version"[^{}]*\}', section.group(1), re.DOTALL)
    25	        if m:
    26	            return m.group(0)
    27	    return None
    28	
    29	
    30	def extract_js(text: str) -> Optional[str]:
    31	    """Extract JavaScript content from model output."""
    32	    js_blocks = re.findall(r"```(?:javascript|js)\s*(.*?)\s*```", text, re.DOTALL)
    33	    if js_blocks:
    34	        return max(js_blocks, key=len).strip()
    35	    return None
    36	
    37	
    38	def extract_json_blocks(text: str) -> list[str]:
    39	    """Extract all JSON code blocks from text."""
    40	    return re.findall(r"```json\s*(\{[^}]*(?:\{[^}]*\}[^}]*)*\})", text, re.DOTALL)
    41	
    42	
    43	def extract_js_blocks(text: str) -> list[str]:
    44	    """Extract all JS code blocks from text."""
    45	    return re.findall(r"```(?:javascript|js)\s*([\s\S]*?)```", text)
    46	
    47	
    48	def extract_all_sections(text: str) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    49	    """Extract structured sections (manifest, JS) from completion."""
    50	    sections = {"manifest": [], "js": []}
    51	    for block in extract_json_blocks(text):
    52	        if "format_version" in block or "header" in block or "modules" in block:
    53	            sections["manifest"].append(block)
    54	    sections["js"] = extract_js_blocks(text)
    55	    return sections
    56	
    57	
    58	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    59	# Individual reward components
    60	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    61	
    62	
    63	def score_structural_alignment(completion: str, reference: str) -> float:
    64	    """Score how well the completion matches the reference structure.
    65	
    66	    Checks: manifest field overlap, JS function overlap, control flow similarity.
    67	    Weight: 35% of total reward.
    68	    """
    69	    ref_sections = extract_all_sections(reference)
    70	    comp_sections = extract_all_sections(completion)
    71	    score = 0.0
    72	    total_weight = 0.0
    73	
    74	    if ref_sections["manifest"]:
    75	        total_weight += 0.4
    76	        ref_manifest = ref_sections["manifest"][0] if ref_sections["manifest"] else ""
    77	        comp_manifest = comp_sections["manifest"][0] if comp_sections["manifest"] else ""
    78	
    79	        if comp_manifest:
    80	            # Field overlap
    81	            ref_fields = set(re.findall(r'"(\w+)":', ref_manifest))
    82	            comp_fields = set(re.findall(r'"(\w+)":', comp_manifest))
    83	            field_match = len(ref_fields & comp_fields) / max(len(ref_fields | comp_fields), 1)
    84	
    85	            # Version match
    86	            ref_ver = re.search(r'format_version["\s:]+([0-9.]+)', ref_manifest)
    87	            comp_ver = re.search(r'format_version["\s:]+([0-9.]+)', comp_manifest)
    88	            ver_match = 1.0 if (ref_ver and comp_ver and ref_ver.group(1) == comp_ver.group(1)) else 0.5
    89	
    90	            score += 0.4 * (0.7 * field_match + 0.3 * ver_match)
    91	
    92	    if ref_sections["js"]:
    93	        total_weight += 0.35
    94	        ref_js = " ".join(ref_sections["js"])
    95	        comp_js = " ".join(comp_sections["js"]) if comp_sections["js"] else ""
    96	
    97	        if comp_js:
    98	            # Function name overlap
    99	            ref_funcs = set(re.findall(r"function\s+(\w+)", ref_js))
   100	            comp_funcs = set(re.findall(r"function\s+(\w+)", comp_js))
   101	            func_match = (
   102	                len(ref_funcs & comp_funcs) / max(len(ref_funcs | comp_funcs), 1)
   103	                if ref_funcs
   104	                else 0
   105	            )
   106	
   107	            # Control flow similarity
   108	            ref_controls = len(re.findall(r"\b(if|for|while|switch)\b", ref_js))
   109	            comp_controls = len(re.findall(r"\b(if|for|while|switch)\b", comp_js))
   110	            control_ratio = min(comp_controls / max(ref_controls, 1), 1.0) if ref_controls else 0.5
   111	
   112	            score += 0.35 * (0.5 * func_match + 0.5 * control_ratio)
   113	
   114	    return score / max(total_weight, 1.0) if total_weight > 0 else 0.0
   115	
   116	
   117	def score_length_ratio(completion: str, reference: str) -> float:
   118	    """Score based on output length relative to reference.
   119	
   120	    Weight: 20% of total reward.
   121	    """
   122	    ref_len = len(reference)
   123	    comp_len = len(completion)
   124	    if ref_len == 0:
   125	        return 0.0
   126	    ratio = comp_len / ref_len
   127	    return min(ratio, 2.0) / 2.0
   128	
   129	
   130	def score_json_validity(completion: str) -> float:
   131	    """Score whether output contains valid JSON.
   132	
   133	    Weight: 25% of total reward.
   134	    """
   135	    for block in extract_json_blocks(completion):
   136	        try:
   137	            json.loads(block)
   138	            return 1.0
   139	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
   140	            pass
   141	    return 0.0
   142	
   143	
   144	def score_content_density(completion: str) -> float:
   145	    """Score how much actual code content the output contains.
   146	
   147	    Weight: 20% of total reward.
   148	    """
   149	    code_blocks = re.findall(r"```[\s\S]*?```", completion)
   150	    if not code_blocks:
   151	        return 0.0
   152	    total_chars = sum(len(b) for b in code_blocks)
   153	    return min(total_chars / 500.0, 1.0)
   154	
   155	
   156	def score_bleu_like(reference: str, hypothesis: str) -> float:
   157	    """Simple BLEU-like F1 score for text overlap."""
   158	    ref_text = re.sub(r"```[^`]*```", "", reference)
   159	    hyp_text = re.sub(r"```[^`]*```", "", hypothesis)
   160	    ref_tokens = set(re.sub(r"[^\w\s]", " ", ref_text).lower().split())
   161	    hyp_tokens = set(re.sub(r"[^\w\s]", " ", hyp_text).lower().split())
   162	
   163	    if not hyp_tokens or not ref_tokens:
   164	        return 0.0
   165	
   166	    overlap = len(ref_tokens & hyp_tokens)
   167	    precision = overlap / len(hyp_tokens)
   168	    recall = overlap / len(ref_tokens)
   169	
   170	    if precision + recall == 0:
   171	        return 0.0
   172	    return 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)
   173	
   174	
   175	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
   176	# Composite reward function
   177	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
   178	
   179	# Reward weights: [structural, length, json_validity, content_density]
   180	REWARD_WEIGHTS = [0.35, 0.20, 0.25, 0.20]
   181	
   182	
   183	def compute_reward(completion: str, reference: str) -> float:
   184	    """Compute composite reward for a completion against reference.
   185	
   186	    Components:
   187	      - Structural alignment (35%): Manifest/JS structure matching
   188	      - Length ratio (20%): Output length vs reference
   189	      - JSON validity (25%): Valid JSON in manifest
   190	      - Content density (20%): Code block density
   191	
   192	    Returns float in [0.0, 1.0].
   193	    """
   194	    completion_text = completion if isinstance(completion, str) else str(completion)
   195	    reference_text = reference if isinstance(reference, str) else str(reference)
   196	
   197	    scores = [
   198	        score_structural_alignment(completion_text, reference_text),
   199	        score_length_ratio(completion_text, reference_text),
   200	        score_json_validity(completion_text),
   201	        score_content_density(completion_text),
   202	    ]
   203	
   204	    return sum(w * s for w, s in zip(REWARD_WEIGHTS, scores))
   205	
   206	
   207	def compute_reward_with_bleu(completion: str, reference: str) -> float:
   208	    """Extended reward with BLEU component (6 components).
   209	
   210	    Components:
   211	      - Structural alignment: 25%
   212	      - BLEU-like overlap: 15%
   213	      - Length ratio: 15%
   214	      - JSON validity: 25%
   215	      - Content density: 20%
   216	    """
   217	    completion_text = completion if isinstance(completion, str) else str(completion)
   218	    reference_text = reference if isinstance(reference, str) else str(reference)
   219	
   220	    scores = [
   221	        score_structural_alignment(completion_text, reference_text),
   222	        score_bleu_like(reference_text, completion_text),
   223	        score_length_ratio(completion_text, reference_text),
   224	        score_json_validity(completion_text),
   225	        score_content_density(completion_text),
   226	    ]
   227	    weights = [0.25, 0.15, 0.15, 0.25, 0.20]
   228	
   229	    return sum(w * s for w, s in zip(weights, scores))
   230	
   231	
   232	def compute_diversity_metrics(completions: list[str]) -> dict:
   233	    """Compute diversity metrics across a group of completions."""
   234	    if len(completions) < 2:
   235	        return {"unique_ratio": 0.0, "avg_length": 0.0, "length_std": 0.0}
   236	
   237	    import numpy as np
   238	
   239	    lengths = [len(c) for c in completions]
   240	    all_bigrams = set()
   241	    for c in completions:
   242	        words = c.split()
   243	        bigrams = [tuple(words[i : i + 2]) for i in range(len(words) - 1)]
   244	        all_bigrams.update(bigrams)
   245	
   246	    total_bigrams = sum(len(c.split()) - 1 for c in completions)
   247	    unique_ratio = len(all_bigrams) / max(total_bigrams, 1)
   248	
   249	    return {
   250	        "unique_ratio": unique_ratio,
   251	        "avg_length": float(np.mean(lengths)),
   252	        "length_std": float(np.std(lengths)) if len(lengths) > 1 else 0.0,
   253	        "num_completions": len(completions),
   254	    }
   255	
   256	
   257	if __name__ == "__main__":
   258	    # Quick test
   259	    test_completion = '''

   262

   264	    ```json

   268	            "name": "test_mod",
   269	            "description": "Test mod",
   270	            "uuid": "abc-123",
   271	            "version": [1, 0, 0],
   272	            "min_engine_version": [1, 20, 0]

{"command":"# Run GRPO v4 from Stage B SFT v2 checkpoint with BLEU-weighted reward
export $(grep TINKER_API_KEY /home/alex/Projects/portkit/.env) && cd /home/alex/Projects/portkit && .venv/bin/python -c "
import asyncio, json, chz
import tinker
from tinker_cookbook import model_info
from tinker_cookbook.rl import train as rl_train
from tinker_cookbook.rl.types import RLDataset, RLDatasetBuilder, Env, EnvGroupBuilder, StepResult
from tinker_cookbook.renderers import get_renderer, Message
from tinker_cookbook.tokenizer_utils import get_tokenizer
from datetime import datetime
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, 'ai-engine/mmsd/tinker')
from reward import compute_reward_with_bleu

model_name = 'Qwen/Qwen3-8B'
renderer_name = model_info.get_recommended_renderer_name(model_name)
tokenizer = get_tokenizer(model_name)
renderer = get_renderer(renderer_name, tokenizer)

# Use filtered Stage B data (MMSD only, no general code for GRPO)
conversations = []
with open('ai-engine/mmsd/tinker/data/stage_b_train_filtered.jsonl') as f:
    for line in f:
        if line.strip():
            conversations.append(json.loads(line))

prompts_data = []
for conv in conversations:
    msgs, reference = [], ''
    for msg in conv['messages']:
        if msg['role'] == 'assistant': reference = msg['content']
        else: msgs.append(msg)
    prompts_data.append((msgs, reference))
print(f'Loaded {len(prompts_data)} prompts (filtered, no general mix)')

class PortKitEnv(Env):
    def __init__(self, messages, reference, renderer):
        self.messages = [Message(role=m['role'], content=m['content']) for m in messages]
        self.reference = reference
        self.renderer = renderer
        self.tokenizer = renderer.tokenizer

    async def initial_observation(self):
        prompt = self.renderer.build_generation_prompt(self.messages)
        return prompt, self.renderer.get_stop_sequences()

    async def step(self, action, *, extra=None):
        response = self.tokenizer.decode(action, skip_special_tokens=True)
        reward = compute_reward_with_bleu(response, self.reference)
        return StepResult(reward=reward, episode_done=True, next_observation=tinker.ModelInput.from_ints([]), next_stop_condition=[])

class PortKitEnvGroupBuilder(EnvGroupBuilder):
    def __init__(self, messages, reference, renderer, group_size=8):
        self.messages, self.reference, self.renderer, self.group_size = messages, reference, renderer, group_size
    async def make_envs(self):
        return [PortKitEnv(self.messages, self.reference, self.renderer) for _ in range(self.group_size)]

@chz.chz
class PortKitRLDatasetBuilder(RLDatasetBuilder):
    renderer_name: str = renderer_name
    model_name_for_tokenizer: str = model_name
    batch_size: int = 8
    group_size: int = 8
    seed: int = 42

    async def __call__(self):
        import random
        rnd = random.Random(self.seed)
        _renderer = get_renderer(self.renderer_name, get_tokenizer(self.model_name_for_tokenizer))
        builders = [PortKitEnvGroupBuilder(msgs, ref, _renderer, self.group_size) for msgs, ref in prompts_data]
        rnd.shuffle(builders)
        train_builders = builders[:int(len(builders) * 0.9)]
        class SimpleRLDataset(RLDataset):
            def __init__(self, data, bs):
                self.data, self.bs = data, bs
            def get_batch(self, index):
                return self.data[index*self.bs:(index+1)*self.bs]
            def __len__(self):
                return len(self.data) // self.bs
        train_ds = SimpleRLDataset(train_builders, self.batch_size)
        print(f'Train batches: {len(train_ds)}')
        return train_ds, None

timestamp = datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')
log_path = f'ai-engine/mmsd/tinker/logs/grpo4_stageb_v2_qwen3-8b_{timestamp}'

# Load from Stage B SFT v2 checkpoint (filtered + general mix)
stageb_v2_checkpoint = 'tinker://8beb3d6b-263b-55ff-955e-67b704cc2b7d:train:0/weights/final'

config = chz.Blueprint(rl_train.Config).apply({
    'log_path': log_path,
    'model_name': model_name,
    'renderer_name': renderer_name,
    'dataset_builder': PortKitRLDatasetBuilder(),
    'learning_rate': 3e-5,
    'max_tokens': 2048,
    'lora_rank': 64,
    'temperature': 0.7,
    'save_every': 25,
    'eval_every': 0,
    'max_steps': 100,
    'load_checkpoint_path': stageb_v2_checkpoint,
})

print(f'GRPO v4 from Stage B v2 checkpoint')
print(f'  Checkpoint: {stageb_v2_checkpoint}')
print(f'  Reward: compute_reward_with_bleu (BLEU 15%, structural 25%)')
print(f'  Steps: 100, Batch: 8, Group: 8, Max tokens: 2048, LR: 3e-5')
print(f'  Log: {log_path}')

config_obj = config.make()
asyncio.run(rl_train.main(config_obj))
print(f'GRPO v4 complete! Logs at {log_path}')

import json, sys
sys.path.insert(0, 'ai-engine/mmsd/tinker')
from reward import compute_reward, compute_reward_with_bleu
from tinker_cookbook import model_info
from tinker_cookbook.renderers import get_renderer, Message
from tinker_cookbook.tokenizer_utils import get_tokenizer
import tinker

model_name = 'Qwen/Qwen3-8B'
renderer_name = model_info.get_recommended_renderer_name(model_name)
tokenizer = get_tokenizer(model_name)
renderer = get_renderer(renderer_name, tokenizer)

eval_data = []
with open('ai-engine/mmsd/tinker/data/stage_b_val_filtered.jsonl') as f:
    for line in f:
        if line.strip():
            eval_data.append(json.loads(line))
print(f'Evaluating on {len(eval_data)} held-out samples')

sc = tinker.ServiceClient()
sp = tinker.SamplingParams(max_tokens=2048, temperature=0.0, stop=renderer.get_stop_sequences())

def eval_checkpoint(name, checkpoint_path):
    print(f'\n=== {name} ===')
    if checkpoint_path:
        client = sc.create_sampling_client(model_path=checkpoint_path)
    else:
        client = sc.create_sampling_client(model_path=None, base_model=model_name)
    
    rewards = []
    bleu_rewards = []
    for i, sample in enumerate(eval_data):
        msgs = [Message(role=m['role'], content=m['content']) for m in sample['messages'] if m['role'] != 'assistant']
        reference = next(m['content'] for m in sample['messages'] if m['role'] == 'assistant')
        prompt = renderer.build_generation_prompt(msgs)
        result = client.sample(prompt, num_samples=1, sampling_params=sp).result()
        response = tokenizer.decode(result.sequences[0].tokens, skip_special_tokens=True)
        
        reward = compute_reward(response, reference)
        bleu_reward = compute_reward_with_bleu(response, reference)
        rewards.append(reward)
        bleu_rewards.append(bleu_reward)
        print(f'  Sample {i:2d}: reward={reward:.4f}, bleu_reward={bleu_reward:.4f}, len={len(response)}', flush=True)
    
    avg = sum(rewards)/len(rewards)
    avg_bleu = sum(bleu_rewards)/len(bleu_rewards)
    print(f'  AVG: reward={avg:.4f}, bleu_reward={avg_bleu:.4f}')
    return avg, avg_bleu

results = {}
results['Baseline'] = eval_checkpoint('Baseline', None)
results['GRPO_v3'] = eval_checkpoint('GRPO v3', 'tinker://ffa0bfc7-f373-5af3-aeab-9773784a51a0:train:0/sampler_weights/final')
results['GRPO_v4'] = eval_checkpoint('GRPO v4', 'tinker://8d9803f1-4a5f-5bbf-ad25-9a221cca7b8b:train:0/sampler_weights/final')

print('\n=== FINAL COMPARISON ===')
print(f'{"Model":<12} {"Reward":>8} {"BLEU-Reward":>12}')
for name, (avg, avg_bleu) in results.items():
    print(f'{name:<12} {avg:>8.4f} {avg_bleu:>12.4f}')
print('DONE', flush=True)
PYEOF

import httpx
from typing import Optional, Dict
from mmsd.validators.code_validator import CodeValidator


class DualTeacherPipeline:
    """
    Synthesizes parallel Java and Bedrock modding codebases with reasoning traces.
    """

    def __init__(self, model: str = "qwen2.5-coder:3b"):
        self.model = model
        self.url = "http://localhost:11434/api/generate"
        self.validator = CodeValidator()

    def synthesize_pair(self, instruction: str) -> Optional[Dict]:
        """
        Generates a reasoning trace and then implementation for both platforms.
        Includes a self-correction loop for common structural failures.
        Returns None if any stage fails with an unrecoverable error.
        """
        print(f"\n--- Synthesizing: {instruction[:50]}... ---")

        # 1. Reasoning Trace
        reasoning_prompt = (
            f"Mod Request: {instruction}\n\n"
            f"Task: Explain how to implement this mod in both Minecraft Java (Forge) and Bedrock (Scripting API). "
            f"Identify the specific Java classes/events and the corresponding Bedrock JSON components/Script events. "
            f"Focus on the functional mapping between the two platforms."
        )
        reasoning_trace = self._query_ollama(
            reasoning_prompt, "You are a master Minecraft architect."
        )
        if not reasoning_trace or reasoning_trace.startswith("Error:"):
            print(f"  SKIP: Reasoning trace failed: {reasoning_trace}")
            return None

        # 2. Java Generation
        java_source = self._generate_with_retry("java", reasoning_trace, instruction)
        if not java_source or java_source.startswith("Error:"):
            print(f"  SKIP: Java generation failed: {java_source}")
            return None

        # 3. Bedrock Generation
        bedrock_source = self._generate_with_retry("bedrock", reasoning_trace, instruction)
        if not bedrock_source or bedrock_source.startswith("Error:"):
            print(f"  SKIP: Bedrock generation failed: {bedrock_source}")
            return None

        return {
            "instruction": instruction,
            "reasoning_trace": reasoning_trace,
            "java_source": java_source,
            "bedrock_source": bedrock_source,
        }

    def _generate_with_retry(
        self, platform: str, plan: str, instruction: str, max_retries: int = 3
    ) -> str:
        if platform == "java":
            system = "You are a senior Java Minecraft modder."

                f"Task: Generate the complete Java source code for a Forge 1.21 mod. "
                f"CRITICAL: You MUST include a 'package com.example.mod;' declaration at the top. "
                f"Include imports and the main class logic. Respond with ONLY the code block."
            )
            validator_fn = self.validator.validate_java
        else:
            system = "You are a senior Bedrock Add-on creator."
            prompt = (
                f"Reasoning Plan: {plan}\n\n"
                f"Task: Generate the Bedrock Add-on files. Include the manifest.json and the main scripting .js file. "

            )
            validator_fn = self.validator.validate_bedrock_json

messages.content:
Now I have all the data needed. Here's the prioritized plan:

---

## Next Steps Plan (Priority Order)

### What we learned from this session

**Key findings from the analysis:**

1. **Reward function is miscalibrated.** Ground truth self-scores only 0.50 on `compute_reward` and 0.57 on `compute_reward_with_bleu` — yet the model scores 0.72/0.74. The model is "reward hacking" by generating outputs that score well on format/structure but don't match ground truth content.

2. **Ground truth JSON is invalid.** 100% of ground truth JSON blocks fail `json.loads()` — they're either truncated or use non-standard Bedrock manifest schemas. The `json_validity` component (25% weight) always returns 0.0 for ground truth but the model gets 1.0 by generating different (valid) JSON. This inflates model scores.

3. **Data is synthetic from Ollama 3B.** All 1,400 MMSD pairs were generated by a local Qwen 2.5 Coder 3B via Ollama — not from real Java→Bedrock conversions. The Bedrock code it produced is hallucinated (fake APIs like `event.level.createLightningBolt()`, incorrect module schemas). This is the ceiling on output quality.

4. **24% of ground truth exceeds 2048 chars** but 0% exceed 2048 tokens. The 2048 max_tokens in GRPO isn't truncating.

5. **Model is above ground truth ceiling** on composite reward (0.72 vs 0.50) — meaning the reward can't discriminate good from great outputs anymore.

---

### Priority 1: Fix the Reward Function
**Cost:** $0 | **Time:** 30 min

The reward is the single biggest lever. Right now it can't tell good from bad because:
- `json_validity` (25% weight) always scores 0 for ground truth (broken JSON) but 1.0 for model (valid JSON)
- `structural_alignment` only checks field name overlap, not semantic correctness
- `bleu` component strips code blocks before comparing (comparing only prose text)

**Actions:**
1. Fix `extract_json_blocks` regex to capture complete multi-level nested JSON
2. Change `json_validity` to check for Bedrock manifest structure (`format_version`, `modules`) instead of strict `json.loads`
3. Rewrite `bleu` to compare code content (inside code blocks), not prose
4. Add `js_api_correctness` component: check for real `@minecraft/server` API usage vs hallucinated APIs
5. Normalize reward so ground truth self-score = 1.0

### Priority 2: Better Synthetic Data with GPT-4o/Claude via Tinker
**Cost:** ~$10-20 in API calls (not Tinker) | **Time:** 2-4 hours

Current data was generated by a local 3B model producing hallucinated Bedrock APIs. Regenerate with a stronger model.

**Actions:**
1. Take 200 diverse instructions from `instructions.jsonl`
2. Use GPT-4o or Claude via the PortKit API to generate high-quality Java→Bedrock pairs
3. Focus on correct `@minecraft/server` API usage and valid Bedrock manifest v2 schema
4. Validate with Bedrock documentation (e.g., `world.afterEvents`, `BlockComponent`, etc.)
5. Mix: 200 high-quality pairs + 1,000 best existing pairs

**Alternative (no API cost):** Use Tinker to sample from the current fine-tuned model, then manually/automatically filter for correct API usage. ~$5 in Tinker sampling costs.

### Priority 3: Curriculum GRPO with Fixed Reward
**Cost:** ~$20-25 | **Time:** 90 min

With the fixed reward from Priority 1, run GRPO with a curriculum:
- Phase 1: 50 steps on easy pairs (short outputs, simple mods)
- Phase 2: 50 steps on hard pairs (longer outputs, complex mods)
- Use `max_tokens=4096` to allow longer completions
- Lower temperature (0.5) for more precise outputs

### Priority 4: DPO with Best-vs-Worst Sampling
**Cost:** ~$10-15 (SFT) + ~$20-25 (DPO) | **Time:** 2 hours

Instead of GRPO (which optimizes for a reward that may still be imperfect), use DPO which directly learns from preference pairs:
1. Sample 4 completions per prompt from the current best model
2. Rank them by the fixed reward
3. Best completion = `chosen`, worst = `rejected`
4. Train DPO on these pairs

DPO is more robust to reward misspecification than GRPO because it learns relative preferences, not absolute scores.

### Priority 5: Real Conversion Data from PortKit Pipeline
**Cost:** $0 (uses existing PortKit infra) | **Time:** 4-8 hours

The PortKit B2B product at modporter.ai does actual Java→Bedrock conversions. Capture real conversions:

**Actions:**
1. Add logging to PortKit's LangGraph pipeline to capture successful conversion pairs
2. Run 50-100 real mod conversions through the pipeline (using GPT-4o as teacher)
3. These will have correct Bedrock API usage and valid manifest schemas
4. Mix 50-100 real pairs into training data (high signal-to-noise)

### Priority 6: Model Architecture Upgrade
**Cost:** ~$30-40 | **Time:** 3 hours

If Qwen3-8B is still plateauing:
1. Try **Qwen3-8B with thinking disabled** (`/no_think` in prompt) — the model may waste tokens on chain-of-thought instead of generating code
2. Try a **code-specific model** if Tinker adds support (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B)
3. Try **LoRA rank 128** instead of 64 for more capacity

---

### Recommended Execution Order with $125 Budget

| Order | Step | Cost | Cumulative |
|-------|------|------|------------|
| 1 | Fix reward function | $0 | $0 |
| 2 | Regenerate 200 HQ pairs (Claude API) | ~$15 | $15 |
| 3 | Retrain SFT v3 (filtered + HQ data) | ~$5 | $20 |
| 4 | GRPO v5 with fixed reward (100 steps) | ~$25 | $45 |
| 5 | DPO with preference pairs | ~$35 | $80 |
| 6 | GRPO v6 curriculum (if budget allows) | ~$25 | $105 |
| 7 | Export + evaluate final model | ~$5 | $110 |
| **Buffer** | | | **$15 remaining** |

**Stop condition:** If BLEU-reward exceeds 0.85 on held-out eval, the model is production-ready. Export and deploy.
